correctness.rationale: The frozen result counts two-dimensional vector subspaces with exactly four rational members, each geometrically smooth. The fresh exact reproduction checks rank 13 of the planar evaluation map in degree five and rank 8 of A↦det(X,X^[3],AX), with scalar kernel. At a rational point p its differential is det(v,p,Ap), so a rational eigenline forces a singularity. The converse follows from Homma–Kim Theorem 3.2 and was separately checked by computing all three affine singularity ideals of representatives of the two no-rational-eigenline form orbits (432 and 144). The complete independent RREF sweep checks all 896260 two-spaces, accepts exactly 2016, and full enumeration of the projective group of order 5616 gives orbit sizes 1872 and 144 and stabilizers 3 and 39 for the displayed representatives. Rational base points are transverse: dependent differentials over F3 would give a singular rational member. Smooth independent degree-five curves have no common component, so Bézout leaves length 12 after those 13 points. Exact chart Gröbner checks give eliminants Z(Z−1)(Z+1) times the frozen irreducible P12 or P3^4, respectively. On that residual locus Z³−Z is a unit and the Gröbner relation is linear in the other coordinate, so the localized quotient is respectively F3[Z]/(P12) or F3[Z]/(P3^4). This certifies Frobenius support and scheme length, not just point counts in a sampled extension; the total Bézout length excludes extra support at infinity. The reduced case additionally has unit base-intersection Jacobian ideal on all three charts. Finally the differential from any system to a fixed rational point's two-dimensional cotangent space has nonzero kernel in vector dimension at least three, ruling out higher-dimensional rationally all-smooth systems.
residual_risks: The completeness is for the stated F3 space and rational pencil members only. No smoothness claim is inferred for every parameter over the algebraic closure; no formal proof or external attestation channel was used.

evidence: The inverse image of an all-smooth pencil in M3(F3) is a three-dimensional subspace S containing I with every nonzero member invertible: det(A−λI)≠0 for each λ∈F3 iff the coset form is smooth. Choosing a nonzero e, evaluation at e maps S bijectively to F3³, so S is a unital semifield's multiplication spread set. Projective pencil equivalence is conjugacy of S, not just arbitrary two-sided linear equivalence.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: In this specific order, isotopy does account for the two conjugacy types after an additional normalization argument. Menichetti's field/twisted-field classification gives the multiplication spread up to S=P S0 Q. Having I in S forces Q=T⁻¹P⁻¹ with T in S0 nonzero. In the field model S0 T⁻¹=S0. For the order-27 twisted model take L_a(x)=a³x+a x³ on K=F27. The general nonfield twist xy−c x^(3^i)y^(3^j) has {i,j}={1,2} and norm(c)≠1; a Frobenius change in one input makes the two terms crossed and an input scaling makes the coefficient sign positive since the kernel of the norm K*→F3* is the squares and norm(c)=−1. Exponent 9 instead of 3 is equivalent by output Frobenius. Writing M_b for scalar multiplication by b∈K*, L_ba=M_(b^4)L_a M_b⁻¹, so S0 L_b⁻¹ is conjugate to S0 L_1⁻¹ for all b≠0. Thus the prior algebraic classification yields at most two normalized conjugacy orbits; the commuting field representative and noncommuting other representative distinguish them. It does not give the claimed intersection schemes.

value.rationale: The natural family of maximally dimensional smooth pencils through the entire rational plane has identical rational base geometry and total intersection length, yet in its two orbits the residual scheme differs in both Frobenius support and geometric multiplicity. Determining that joint invariant exactly is useful independently of the older algebraic classification: it specifies the nonrational centers and their scheme thickness for the two types, data a computation of the spread sets or of individual-curve invariants does not by itself provide. This is not value assigned solely to recounting the conjugacy orbits.
residual_risks: The residual dichotomy is established for the fixed F3 minimal-degree system, not proposed as universal for other fields or degrees.
